name: fig_lean_scaling
title: Lean checker runtime vs document size
question: How does the compiled Lean checker's wall time grow with the number of mandatory requirements and coupled constraints, and what does batching buy?
model: Wall-clock timing (time.perf_counter) of lean_runner.check (one Lean process per check), of the Lean process alone on a pre-written input, and of lean_runner.check_batch over 100 identical pairs (per pair); median and IQR of 7 interleaved repeats after warm-up; OLS fit of log10(time) on log10(size) over the upper decade, 95% CI from the t distribution.
data: paper/data/bench_lean_scaling.json (raw timings) and paper/data/fig_lean_scaling.json (summaries), written by paper/scripts/fig_benchmarks.py. (a) SYNTHETIC documents: N = 1..2000 mandatory requirements over N matching documented capabilities (5 constraint shapes, all pass; Lean verdict REQUIREMENTS_MET for every N). (b) the real Demo B documents (quantum_mxc_wiring_heat_budget on bluefors_ld400_hdw) with the real mxc_wiring_heat_budget relation repeated k = 1..1000 times (Lean verdict DOES_NOT_MEET_REQUIREMENTS for every k: each copy fails as in Demo B); batches only up to k = 200. Machine: Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-14900HX (24 cores / 32 threads, 29.7 GiB), Windows-11-10.0.26200-SP0, Python 3.12.10, cryolean v2 (Lean 4.35.0), Z3 5.3.3.
caption: Wall time of the compiled Lean checker per experiment-configuration check versus (a) the number of mandatory requirements in synthetic documents and (b) the number of coupled constraints (the real Demo B heat-budget relation repeated). Points are the 7 repeats, markers the median, bars the IQR; the grey band is the Lean process start (cryolean version, median 99 ms). One process per check costs 142 ms at N = 1 and 382 ms at N = 2000 (upper-decade log-log slope 0.36 [0.23, 0.48]), because process start dominates; inside a 100-pair batch the per-pair cost rises from 1.4 ms to 341 ms (slope 1.20 [1.12, 1.28]), so the advantage of batching shrinks from 99x at N = 1 to 1.12x at N = 2000. Coupled constraints cost more per item (954 ms for k = 1000; slopes 0.64 [0.53, 0.74] single, 1.06 [0.97, 1.15] batch). Dashed lines are power-law fits over the upper decade. All times are measured; verdicts come from the Lean checker. The machine was not idle: median whole-system CPU utilisation during this benchmark was 38% (other desktop applications, antivirus scanning and other sessions' jobs).
